conventions.convention: Fields use one SI inertial laboratory frame. Permittivity and permeability are static, measurable, essentially bounded, real symmetric matrix fields with uniform positive lower bounds.
Admissible bulk fields belong to C1(I;L2) intersect C(I;H(curl)); Maxwell evolution holds as an L2 identity at every time. PEC means graph-norm closure of compactly supported smooth electric fields.
Boundary area is the finite Borel measure obtained by summing planar face areas, with edges and vertices null. Boundary-time integration uses its product with Lebesgue measure on I.

The normal is outward and the cross product is right-handed. The impedance law is Hτ = Y(n × Eτ), with Y ≥ 0, so outward power is Y|Eτ|². Boundary fields are separately supplied L2 data satisfying the displayed scalar Green identity; no general trace theorem is asserted.
On a compact embedded C2 surface without boundary, weak surface divergence acts by DivS K(φ) = −∫S K·∇Sφ dS. Pointwise divergence requires a proved continuous-density representation.
The sheet is fixed, its normal points from minus to plus, and [F] = F+ − F−. Fields and volume sources have the stated joint one-sided C1 extensions; the sheet current is tangential.

These are conditional model deductions, without empirical measurements or material-realization claims. The point-charge counterexample concerns ordinary unregularized quadratic field energy for q ≠ 0.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the static uniformly positive coefficient Maxwell evolution class, its finite quadratic energy, the closure-defined PEC branch, and an impedance branch carrying separately specified tangential L2 boundary data satisfying the displayed Green identity and Hτ = Y(n × Eτ). It asserts no existence or general L2 trace theorem.

For every s < t in I, PEC gives W(t) − W(s) = −∫sᵗ∫Ω E·J, and the Green-compatible impedance branch adds −∫sᵗ∫∂Ω Y|Eτ|². If J = 0 and E(t0) = H(t0) = 0 in L2, the only admissible solution is zero for t ≥ t0.

For an integrable tangential field K on the stated compact C2 surface, define DivS K by its action −∫S K·∇Sφ on C1 scalar tests. The definition does not itself assert existence or uniqueness of a continuous density.
Assuming ACω, a C1 tangential field on a compact embedded C2 hypersurface without boundary has a unique continuous weak-divergence density, with chart formula g(X(u)) = JX(u)⁻¹ Σa ∂a(JX Ka)(u).
Under the stated stationary-interface regularity and distributional macroscopic Maxwell assumptions, n·[D] = σ, n·[B] = 0, n × [E] = 0, n × [H] = K, and ∂tσ + divS K + n·[Jv] = 0 pointwise on S × I.

concerns.concern: The title and physical_scope claim forward initial-value uniqueness, and proof step 5.1 begins 'For the homogeneous difference of two solutions with equal data at t0, linearity gives J=0'. However, the impedance admissibility condition in def-emx-finite-energy-boundary-model is only a quadratic scalar Green identity for each solution and its separately supplied boundary pair. It supplies neither a linear trace map nor cross Green identities, so differences need not be admissible. A concrete counterexample uses Ω=(0,1)^3, I=(-1/4,1/4), and coefficients with SI numerical values ε=μ=Y=1. Put f(s)=1 for s≥0 and f(s)=1−(1/2)exp(−1/s²) for s<0. Both E=e_y,H=e_z and E=f(x−t)e_y,H=f(x−t)e_z solve the homogeneous bulk equations and agree at t=0, but differ for t>0. The second has nonnegative total outward power P(t)=f(1−t)²−f(−t)². Give it the artificial boundary data Eτ=√P(t)e_y on the x=1 face and zero elsewhere, with Hτ=n×Eτ; these satisfy exactly the stipulated Green identity and impedance law. Give the constant solution zero boundary data. Both are admissible under the written definition. Thus general impedance initial-value uniqueness is false for this class. The stated energy identities and the explicitly narrower zero-initial-data conclusion remain valid.

seams_checked.note: Checked the prerequisite page and pthm-emx-oscillator-energy. Its fixed-volume application uses only the PEC energy balance, with constant positive coefficients and effective current Jf plus polarization/carrier current. It explicitly checks the required time and L2 regularity and does not invoke impedance uniqueness.

Checked def-emx-whitney-semidescretization and pthm-emx-coercive-maxwell-galerkin against the supplier. They preserve static positive coefficient and closure-defined PEC conventions. The semidiscretization expressly requires Hh only in L2 and does not claim that it satisfies the continuum H(curl) solution class or inherits its uniqueness theorem.

Checked def-emx-port-scattering-model. It uses the same outward-power sign for classical smooth tangential fields, explicitly avoids inferring L2 traces from H(curl), and independently assumes the fixed-frequency solution map's existence and uniqueness. It does not derive scattering uniqueness from the weak energy theorem.
